idiom_name: pthread_mutex + pthread_cond_timedwait around an ordered pending array
implementation_notes: ISO C ships neither an ordered container nor a resequencer, so the classic structure is written out: a pending array kept sorted by sequence number (or a small hand-rolled binary heap once the window grows), a per-correlation expected counter, and a pthread_mutex_t plus pthread_cond_t guarding them. The gap deadline is a pthread_cond_timedwait with an absolute timespec; on ETIMEDOUT the expected counter is advanced past the hole, which is what prevents the permanent stall. An event-loop variant replaces the mutex and condition variable with a callback plus a timer, but keeps the same window, cursor and gap policy.
pitfalls: pthread_cond_timedwait takes an absolute deadline in struct timespec, not a relative timeout; computing it after taking the lock is what keeps the gap policy from firing early or never.
Delivering while holding the mutex serialises the whole pipeline and deadlocks when the consumer re-enters the resequencer; copy the ready run out and deliver after unlocking.
The pending array must be bounded: a stalled or hostile producer otherwise drives the buffer until memory is exhausted.
Sequence numbers must be an ordered integer type wide enough for the stream; wrapping comparison logic silently turns old messages into new ones.
